svg.aria-label: Lab architecture: repositories flow through PowerShell automation into a pinned, verified Trivy, producing JSON reports with metadata and derived SARIF, SBOM and table formats
svg.title: Trivy blind spots: lab architecture
svg.desc: Four stages. 1 What we scan: target list, remote repositories, local clones (untrusted), known-answer fixtures. 2 Lab automation: bulk scan, single-repository scan, lock-file generator in a hardened container, coverage matrix, all driven by the lab policy in config/. 3 Pinned scanner: Trivy 0.76.1 as a SHA-256 verified native binary, a digest-pinned container or client/server, running vulnerability, secret, misconfiguration and licence scanners. 4 Evidence: a JSON report plus .meta.json, converted without re-scanning to SARIF, SBOM and table.
svg.text: How the lab turns a repository into auditable evidence

g.text: many repos, or a whole GitHub org
one repository, every scanner at once
flags “0 found” when nothing was read
ready for CI, audits and dashboards
WHY THE RESULTS CAN BE TRUSTED
exact Trivy version + SHA-256; images by digest
scripts stay outside the scanned repositories
projects Trivy could not read are flagged
